reviewer: Codex editorial review under the site owner's instruction; each claim checked against cited comments

reviews.summary: Commenters praised the art style [1][3][4], with one singling out the dancing animation [2]. Another liked the Malta setting and historical theme [3]. These are reactions to the showcase: two commenters said they still needed time to play [3][4].

The tornado received praise [1], and a commenter suggested more outlandish settings such as underwater or volcanic levels [4]. A returning player found the controls worse and the game too easy [2]; another reported loading lag on their machine [3]. The HUD was also suggested as an area for visual improvement [5]. These reports describe that version, not a current performance test.

Several reactions favored the move to 3D: commenters liked the added detail [1] and how the destruction looked [2]. One preferred the earlier presentation [3]. Camera navigation was a concern, with a fixed camera suggested as an alternative to a third-person view [4]. These are showcase reactions, not a measured playtest result.

Commenters praised the landscape view [1] and consistency of the art [2]. One suggested cleaning up blurry sprite outlines while continuing to build the game [3]. Another proposed a first-person view for exploring the settlement and entering houses [4].

Commenters appreciated the site’s polish [1] and the browser format and breadth of missions [3]. One wanted more original art and mechanics to distinguish the game from Advance Wars [2]. A small animation detail—the sergeant’s whistle—also drew a suggestion [4]. One commenter explicitly had not assessed the gameplay [1], so these reactions should not be read as completed playtests.

Reactions to the retro visuals varied: one commenter liked their early-nineties feel [1], while another wanted pixelation fixed and gameplay improved [2]. A visitor reported a distorted display and no way to mute the music [3]. A detailed suggestion was to check canvas resolution and device scaling, then make asset palettes and lighting more consistent [4]. That suggestion is advice from a commenter, not a verified diagnosis.
